podcast.body: During Madness's performance of "One Step Beyond" at the Madstock festival on August 18, 1992, the collective dancing ("skanking") of the 36,000+ attendees created vibrations so intense they simulated an earthquake for blocks around. These vibrations were strong enough to register on the Richter scale. "So many people were dancing in skankinger in the song, one step beyond, that they created vibrations that simulated an earthquake for blocks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 1

podcast.body: This song was a significant hit among the 1960s British subculture known as Swadeheds. Madness later covered the track during the ska revival of the late 1970s and early 1980s, bringing it to a new generation. "And of course, madness would cover that song during the sky revival of the late 70s and early 80s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
